"'''Let Me Love You'''" is a song by American singer [[Mario (American singer)|Mario]], released by [[J Records]] on October 4, 2004, as the lead single from his second studio album, ''[[Turning Point (Mario album)|Turning Point]]'' (2004). The song was written by then-unknown American singer [[Ne-Yo]], Kameron Houff, and [[Scott Storch]], while production was handled by the latter. The song garnered Mario a [[Grammy Award]] nomination for [[Grammy Award for Best Male R&B Vocal Performance|Best Male R&B Vocal Performance]] in 2006 and became a top-10 hit worldwide, reaching number one in the United States, Canada, Germany, the Netherlands, and New Zealand.

"Let Me Love You" is considered to be Mario's [[List of signature songs|signature song]], as well as a prominent track in [[Contemporary R&B#2000s|2000s R&B music]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Marie "Let Me Love You" is a song by American singer Mario, released by J Records on October 4, 2004, as the lead single from his second studio album, Turning Point (2004). The song was written by then-unknown American singer Ne-Yo, Kameron Houff, and Scott Storch, while production was handled by the latter. The song garnered Mario a Grammy Award nomination for Best Male R&B Vocal Performance in 2006 and became a top-10 hit worldwide, reaching number one in the United States, Canada, Germany, the Netherlands, and New Zealand.

"Let Me Love You" is considered to be Mario's signature song, as well as a prominent track in 2000s R&B music. In 2008, the song was ranked number 45 on Billboard{{'}}s All-Time Top 100 Hot 100 singles, during the first 50 years of the chart. It was the eighth most successful single of the decade according to the Billboard Hot 100 Songs of the Decade chart released in December 2009. In 2013, it was ranked at number 53 on Billboard{{'}}s All-Time Top 100 Hot 100 singles during the first 55 years of the chart. The remix of the song, also produced by Storch, contains rapped verses from Jadakiss and T.I.. An additional remix was released featuring verses from rapper Cuban Link and was included on Cuban's mixtape Man on Fire.{{citation needed|date=August 2025}}

So most of the records on [''Turning Point''] are uptempo club records. When Ne-Yo came in, we were like, 'We actually need to make some R&B songs for the ladies.'" Ne-Yo revealed during a 2024 interview that he didn't think that Mario was the right performer for "Let Me Love You", because he considered the song's content too mature for an 18-year-old singer.{{Cite web |last=Fekadu |first=Mesfin |date=February 11, 2024 |title=On 20th Anniversary of 'Let Me Love You,' Ne-Yo Recalls Mario Being 'Sam Cooke Reincarnated' Speaking about giving "Let Me Love You" to [[Mario (American singer)|Mario]], Ne-Yo said that "at the time that I wrote it I wasn’t trying to be an artist, I was completely content with just being a [[G minor]], centered around the progression C minor / G minor / F major. It is written in [[common time]].{{cite web|url=http://www.musicnotes.com/download/scorch/default.asp?ppn=SC0022946|title=Download Sheet Music Software – Musicnotes.com|website=Musicnotes}}{{Cite web |date=December 19, 2022 |title=The Number Ones: Mario's 'Let Me Love You' |url=https://www.stereogum.com/2208512/the-number-ones-marios-let-me-love-you/columns/the-number-ones/ |access-date=November 14, 2024 |website=Stereogum |language=en}} ''[[Stereogum]]'' described its instrumental as a "mechanized melodic backbeat with sturdy, clap-heavy drum track and some lost, wandering ’80s-style synth-pillows". The song's lyrical content focuses on the singer's desire to have a romantic relationship with a girl whose current significant other cheats on her. On "Let Me Love You", Mario was noted for portraying "a classic nonthreatening nice-guy type" character, with a [[Michael Jackson]]-inspired vocal performance.

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext:
[[Contactmusic.com]] critic Tareck Ghoneim called "Let Me Love You" an "excellent track that oozes smooth soul, genuine feel good vibes and sing along sentiment as well. The beats have a lazy hip hop beat with soulful bass and seductive keys. It provides a nice and smooth backline for Mario to show what he’s made of and he delivers his soulful vocals with conviction and genuine serenity."<ref>{{cite web|first=Tareck |last=Ghoneim|url=https://www.contactmusic.com/pages/mariox21x03x05|title=Mario – Let Me Love You – Single Review| website=contactmusic.com |date=2005 | access-date=October 17, 2024}}</ref> Caroline Sullivan, writing for ''[[The Guardian]]'' found that the song's "silky exterior encloses a core of smut that's all the more compelling for the [[Alpine climate|Alpine]] purity of Mario's voice."<ref>{{cite web|first=Caroline |last=Sullivan|url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2005/apr/01/popandrock.shopping4|title=Mario, Turning Point| website=[[The Guardian]] |date=April 1, 2005 | access-date=October 17, 2024}}</ref> ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' ranked the song at number seven in their "Top 50 Love Songs of All Time" list.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Bronson |first=Fred |date=February 7, 2024 |title=Top 50 Love Songs of All Time |url=https://www.billboard.com/lists/top-love-songs-all-time/let-me-love-you-mario-hot-100-peak-no-1-for-nine-weeks-2005-2/ |access-date=November 14, 2024 |magazine=Billboard |language=en-US}}</ref> ''[[The Plain Dealer#Cleveland.com|Cleveland.com]]'' commented that the track "does away with any flashy elements, sticking to a classic R&B formula with Mario’s vocals leading the way. This one could have been a hit in any decade".<ref>{{cite news|first= Troy L. |last= Smith |title= Every No. 1 song of the 2000s ranked from worst to best |website= [[Cleveland.com]] |date= September 13, 2021 |access-date= January 31, 2023|url= https://www.cleveland.com/entertainment/2021/09/every-no-1-song-of-the-2000s-ranked-from-worst-to-best.html}}</ref>

In her review of parent album ''Turning Point'', [[BBC Music]]'s Denise Boyd wrote: "The stand out track "Let Me Love You" has already tugged at the heart strings of the R&B audience, becoming a club, party and car stereo anthem on both sides of the Atlantic. Its smooth and soulful narrative sets the tone for much of this album."<ref name="Boyd 2005">{{cite web|first=Denise|last=Boyd|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/music/reviews/z2zf/|title=Mario, Turning Point – Review | website=[[BBC Music]] |date=2005 | access-date=October 17, 2024}}</ref> Jon Pareles from ''[[The New York Times]]'' commented that "Let Me Love You" "looks back to another 1980s blockbuster, lifting its keyboard sound from [[Tina Turner]]'s '[[What's Love Got to Do with It (song)|What's Love Got to Do with It]]'."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2004/12/20/arts/20choi.html|title=CRITIC'S CHOICE New CD's | work=The New York Times | first=Jon | last=Pareles | date=December 20, 2004 | access-date=May 7, 2010}}</ref> ''[[Today (American TV program)|Today]]'' defined the track a "blockbuster hit" and "a passionate plea to take on an elevated role in his crush's life".<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 17, 2024 |title=80 love songs that'll make you feel all the feels |url=https://www.today.com/popculture/music/best-love-songs-rcna39106 |access-date=November 14, 2024 |website=TODAY.com |language=en}}</ref>
sections.text:
Contactmusic.com critic Tareck Ghoneim called "Let Me Love You" an "excellent track that oozes smooth soul, genuine feel good vibes and sing along sentiment as well. The beats have a lazy hip hop beat with soulful bass and seductive keys. It provides a nice and smooth backline for Mario to show what he’s made of and he delivers his soulful vocals with conviction and genuine serenity." Caroline Sullivan, writing for The Guardian found that the song's "silky exterior encloses a core of smut that's all the more compelling for the Alpine purity of Mario's voice." Billboard ranked the song at number seven in their "Top 50 Love Songs of All Time" list. Cleveland.com commented that the track "does away with any flashy elements, sticking to a classic R&B formula with Mario’s vocals leading the way. This one could have been a hit in any decade".

In her review of parent album Turning Point, BBC Music's Denise Boyd wrote: "The stand out track "Let Me Love You" has already tugged at the heart strings of the R&B audience, becoming a club, party and car stereo anthem on both sides of the Atlantic. Its smooth and soulful narrative sets the tone for much of this album." Jon Pareles from The New York Times commented that "Let Me Love You" "looks back to another 1980s blockbuster, lifting its keyboard sound from Tina Turner's 'What's Love Got to Do with It'." Today defined the track a "blockbuster hit" and "a passionate plea to take on an elevated role in his crush's life".

sections.heading: Accolades and nominations
sections.wikitext:
In 2004, "Let Me Love You" was nominated for a [[Vibe Awards|Vibe Award]] for Best R&B Song and two [[Teen Choice Awards]], [[Teen Choice Award for Choice Music – Love Song|Choice Love Song]] and Choice R&B/Rap Track, but it failed to receive any awards. In 2005, it received nominations for [[Billboard Music Award|''Billboard'' Music Awards]], including "Hot 100 Single of the Year", "Hot 100 Airplay Single of the Year", "Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Single of the Year", and "Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Airplay Single of the Year", winning in both of the R&B/Hip-Hop categories. It was also nominated for an MTV Europe Music Award for Best R&B Single, a Viewer's Choice award at the [[BET Awards]], Best Single at the [[MOBO Awards]], and Best R&B/Soul Song at the [[Soul Train Music Awards]]. In 2006, Mario was nominated for a [[Grammy Award]] for [[Grammy Award for Best Male R&B Vocal Performance|Best Male R&B Vocal Performance]] with "Let Me Love You". He also received an [[MTV Australia Awards]] nomination for Best R&B music video for "Let Me Love You".<ref>{{cite news|url=http://theenvelope.latimes.com/factsheets/awardsdb/env-awards-db-search,0,7169155.htmlstory?searchtype=person&query=Mario|title= Mario 2005 BET Awards, Teen Choice Awards & Billboard Music Awards|access-date=January 18, 2009 | work=Los Angeles Times}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://top40.about.com/od/awards/a/billboardma2005_2.htm|title=Billboard Music Award Nominations 2005|access-date=January 25, 2009|archive-date=November 7, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151107054344/http://top40.about.com/od/awards/a/billboardma2005_2.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/61860/usher-50-cent-lead-billboard-rbhip-hop-winners |title=Usher, 50 Cent Lead Billboard R&B/Hip-Hop Winners |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |access-date=January 31, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140922061403/http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/61860/usher-50-cent-lead-billboard-rbhip-hop-winners |archive-date=September 22, 2014 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|access-date=January 18, 2009|url= http://www.rockonthenet.com/artists-m/mario.htm|title= Mario grammy nominations|publisher=Rock on the Net}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/entertainment/4273504.stm

sections.text: In 2004, "Let Me Love You" was nominated for a Vibe Award for Best R&B Song and two Teen Choice Awards, Choice Love Song and Choice R&B/Rap Track, but it failed to receive any awards. In 2005, it received nominations for Billboard Music Awards, including "Hot 100 Single of the Year", "Hot 100 Airplay Single of the Year", "Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Single of the Year", and "Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Airplay Single of the Year", winning in both of the R&B/Hip-Hop categories. It was also nominated for an MTV Europe Music Award for Best R&B Single, a Viewer's Choice award at the BET Awards, Best Single at the MOBO Awards, and Best R&B/Soul Song at the Soul Train Music Awards. In 2006, Mario was nominated for a Grammy Award for Best Male R&B Vocal Performance with "Let Me Love You". He also received an MTV Australia Awards nomination for Best R&B music video for "Let Me Love You".

sections.heading: Commercial performance
sections.wikitext: "Let Me Love You" debuted on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100 the week of October 23, 2004, at number 97. The song went on to hold the number-one position on the U.S. [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] chart for nine consecutive weeks from January to February 2005, and, as of {{YEAR}}, is Mario's biggest single. It also reached number one on the [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs]] chart. Internationally, it reached the number-one position on the singles charts in Germany, the Netherlands, New Zealand and in the continental chart European Hot 100. In the United Kingdom, the song reached number two on the [[UK Singles Chart]] (held off the top spot by "[[(Is This the Way to) Amarillo]]"), making it Mario's biggest hit to date in the UK. The single also holds the honor of being one of the highest-selling ringtones with 1.6 million downloads.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mario2u.com/biography|title=Mario – Top selling ringtones|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080316000930/http://www.mario2u.com/biography|archive-date=March 16, 2008}}</ref>
sections.text: "Let Me Love You" debuted on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100 the week of October 23, 2004, at number 97. The song went on to hold the number-one position on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100 chart for nine consecutive weeks from January to February 2005, and, as of {{YEAR}}, is Mario's biggest single. It also reached number one on the Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart. Internationally, it reached the number-one position on the singles charts in Germany, the Netherlands, New Zealand and in the continental chart European Hot 100. In the United Kingdom, the song reached number two on the UK Singles Chart (held off the top spot by "(Is This the Way to) Amarillo"), making it Mario's biggest hit to date in the UK. The single also holds the honor of being one of the highest-selling ringtones with 1.6 million downloads.
